questions.enonce_markdown:
**Section IV Essay (10 marks)**

**1.** Write a dialogue between a client who wants to have the electric installations in his house done by you the electrician. He does not know what to do so you have to imagine his questions and your responses. You are Noubisse.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Un dialogue rédigé en anglais suit une structure fixe : chaque réplique commence par le nom du locuteur suivi de deux points, les tours de parole s'enchaînent de façon cohérente (chaque réponse doit correspondre logiquement à la question ou à la remarque précédente), et le registre reste adapté à la situation - ici une relation professionnelle client-artisan, donc poli mais direct.

**Corrigé modèle :**

Client: Good morning. I've just moved into this house and I need someone to do all the electric installations. Can you help me?

Noubisse: Good morning, Sir. Yes, of course, that is exactly my job. Could you tell me how many rooms you want wired?

Client: There are five rooms in total: three bedrooms, a sitting room and a kitchen.

Noubisse: Alright. Do you already have a distribution board, or should I install a new one?

Client: I have no idea what a distribution board is, to be honest.

Noubisse: Don't worry, I'll explain. It's the box that controls and protects all the electric circuits in your house. Without it, your appliances could be damaged by a power surge.

Client: I see. So, will I need one?

Noubisse: Yes, definitely. I will install a new distribution board with circuit breakers for safety.

Client: How long will the whole installation take?

Noubisse: If I start tomorrow morning, I should finish within three days, provided the materials are available.

Client: What materials will you need?

Noubisse: Cables, switches, sockets, the distribution board, circuit breakers and light fittings. I can buy them myself if you give me the budget.

Client: That's fine. How much will the whole job cost me?

Noubisse: Including labour and materials, it should come to about 150,000 FCFA. I will give you a written estimate before I start.

Client: Perfect. When can you begin?

Noubisse: I can start first thing tomorrow morning, if that suits you.

Client: That suits me perfectly. Thank you very much.

Noubisse: You are welcome, Sir. See you tomorrow.

### Piège à éviter
Ne fais jamais parler un personnage de façon incohérente avec son rôle : le client (non spécialiste) pose des questions et exprime son ignorance technique, tandis que Noubisse (l'électricien) explique, rassure et propose des solutions - inverser ces rôles est une erreur fréquente qui coûte des points.

### Conseil
Varie les types de répliques (question, réponse, explication, proposition) plutôt que d'enchaîner uniquement des questions-réponses fermées : cela rend le dialogue plus vivant et démontre une meilleure maîtrise de la langue.

questions.enonce_markdown: **2.** Imagine that you have been asked to give a talk during youth week to some young people about the importance of being an electrician. Write the speech that you will make. You will try to tell the young people about the importance of hard work and the benefits that an electrician can have from his profession.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Un discours (*speech*) commence toujours par une formule d'adresse au public (« Dear friends », « Good morning everyone »), suivie d'une brève entrée en matière qui annonce le sujet ; le corps développe deux ou trois idées clairement articulées par des connecteurs logiques (firstly, secondly, finally), et la conclusion relance l'auditoire par un appel à l'action ou un message d'encouragement.

**Corrigé modèle :**

Dear young friends,

Good morning, and thank you for inviting me to speak to you during this youth week. Today, I would like to talk to you about the importance of being an electrician.

Many young people think that becoming an electrician is not a respectable or rewarding career, but I strongly disagree. Firstly, an electrician provides an essential service: without electricity, homes, schools, hospitals and factories simply cannot function. Every building you see around you needed the hard work of an electrician at some point.

Secondly, this profession teaches you the value of hard work. Wiring a house properly demands patience, precision and discipline, because a small mistake can cause a fire or an accident. The habits of care and seriousness that you develop in the workshop will help you in every other area of your life.

Finally, being a qualified electrician brings real benefits. You can work for a company, or you can start your own small business and become your own boss. You will always find work, because people will always need electricity. In my own experience, hard work in this trade has given me both an income and genuine pride in what I do.

So, dear young friends, do not look down on manual and technical trades. Choose a trade like electricity with confidence, work hard at it, and it will reward you for the rest of your life.

Thank you for listening.

### Piège à éviter
Ne rédige jamais un discours comme une simple liste de phrases sans connecteurs (« Firstly… Secondly… Finally… ») : sans ces marqueurs, l'auditoire, et le correcteur, perdent le fil de l'argumentation.

### Conseil
Termine toujours un discours par une phrase qui s'adresse directement au public (un encouragement, un appel à l'action) plutôt que par une simple information : c'est ce qui distingue un discours d'un simple exposé écrit.

questions.enonce_markdown: **3.** Write about 'A day when everything went wrong in the workshop in your college'. State what happened, why it was a sad experience, who suffered and the consequences for your college. In this essay, your name should be Noubisse and your college, Lycée Technique de Koumassi.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Un récit narratif (« A day when… ») suit une structure chronologique claire : une brève introduction qui situe le moment et le lieu, un développement qui raconte les événements dans l'ordre où ils se sont produits (au prétérit, avec des connecteurs temporels comme « first », « then », « suddenly », « finally »), et une conclusion qui tire les conséquences ou la leçon de l'événement raconté.

**Corrigé modèle :**

My name is Noubisse and I am a student at Lycée Technique de Koumassi. I will never forget the day when everything went wrong in our electricity workshop.

It happened on a Wednesday afternoon during our practical class. We were working in groups to wire a small model house as part of our end-of-term project. Everything started well: each group connected its switches, sockets and lamps according to the instructions given by our teacher.

However, around three o'clock, one of my classmates, in a hurry to finish before the bell rang, connected a live wire directly to the mains without switching off the power first. Suddenly, there was a loud bang, sparks flew from the board, and all the lights in the workshop went out. Some of the girls screamed, and thick smoke began to rise from one of the model houses, which caught fire. Our teacher rushed in, unplugged the main switch, and used the fire extinguisher to put out the flames before they could spread further.

Fortunately, no one was injured, but three of the model houses were completely destroyed, along with several tools that had melted in the heat. It was a sad experience, because months of hard work were lost in just a few minutes, and the school had to spend a large amount of money to replace the damaged equipment and repair the wiring of the workshop.

Since that day, our college has become much stricter about safety rules: no student is now allowed to touch a circuit without the teacher's supervision, and everyone must switch off the power at the mains before starting any practical work. Although it was a frightening and costly experience, it taught all of us, students of Lycée Technique de Koumassi, a lesson we will never forget: safety must always come before speed.

### Piège à éviter
N'oublie jamais de répondre à TOUTES les consignes du sujet (ici : ce qui s'est passé, pourquoi c'était triste, qui a souffert, ET les conséquences pour le collège) : un récit bien écrit mais qui omet un de ces éléments perd des points au barème, même s'il est agréable à lire.

### Conseil
Utilise systématiquement le prétérit pour raconter des événements passés et des connecteurs temporels variés (that day, suddenly, a few minutes later, since then) : cela structure ton récit et montre la maîtrise du temps narratif attendue à ce niveau.

rappels_de_methode.competence: Structure d'un récit narratif en anglais

incertitudes: Aucune consigne explicite du type « Choose ONE of the following subjects » n'est imprimée sur le sujet source pour la Section IV Essay, bien que ce soit l'usage standard pour ce type d'épreuve (barème unique de 10 points pour 3 sujets au choix). Par souci d'exhaustivité pédagogique, un corrigé modèle complet a été rédigé pour les 3 sujets proposés plutôt que pour un seul.
